title: A new edge that merges a preexisting SCC introduces the merged SCC's contradiction even though its canonical witness is the old cycle; a call that lifts to no edge keeps the old SCC preexisting

assert.why: A.7.5.1 rule 7: an introduced sound contradiction blocks (tier normal, so rule 2 does not apply)
A.4.4.8: one key per non-trivial SCC of E|calls; the head has the single SCC {A,B,C}

A.7.3.3 [D5] with A.4.4.11 (supports decide introduced): Supp of the merged SCC holds the lifted edge C->A, whose only fact (at the new fc2) is new (A.7.3.1), so the contradiction is introduced although the canonical witness is the old cycle A->B->A; binding = support code fa, fb, fb2, fc2 plus (fc2, own) as the affected finest change (A.7.2.2); sound: callScan is presence-sound (A.4.4.13); tier* normal (A.6.2.3)
A.15.4 and A.4.4.10: the witness is the canonical least cycle through the least node m::A, i.e. A->B->A (2 observed facts before 3), so the new fact is in the support but not in the witness
A.4.4.10: the canonical witness A->B->A contains the fact fa->fb
A.4.4.8: subjects are the head's SCCs; {A,B} is no longer an SCC
A.7.4.2 [D3]: call(ts) is not observable (callScan is not absence-sound in the base) and the claim's tier is not final, so no pair is needed
A.7.5.1 rule 6: only a non-introduced obligation remains

A.7.3.3 [D5]: no supporting lifted edge of {A,B} is new (fc2's call stays inside C and lifts to no edge, A.4.4.2), so preexisting; binding = support code fa, fb with no affected finest change (A.7.2.2)
A.4.4.8: without C->A there is no SCC {A,B,C}
A.7.4.2 [D3]: call(ts) is unobservable and the tier is not final
A.7.7.2: an open non-introduced obligation is listed as preexisting
